name: Shiva Published Studies (3 amygdala + 3 chirp configurations, Swann 2002 timing)
origin: Todd Murphy (Shiva software, 'Published Experiment Session'), modelled on the Laurentian standard circumcerebral protocol (Cook, Koren & Persinger 1999; Persinger, Roll, Tiller, Koren & Cook 2002, the Ingo Swann study)
summary: Todd Murphy's Shiva session after the six configurations of the Persinger lab's psi studies: three with the amygdala signal, then three with his modulated 40 Hz chirp, counter-clockwise around the head with quiet intervals in between, 40-45 min. The per-coil timings, point durations and gaps follow the lab's 'standard protocol' as printed in the Ingo Swann paper (Persinger et al. 2002, Table 1), the set that matches Murphy's description. Murphy calls it a good session to begin with for creating altered states.
notes: Murphy: 'The set of configurations used in the lab studies on psychic phenomena have six phases. The first three use the amygdala signal, and the second three use the chirp signal. There are quiet intervals between them'; the session runs 40 to 45 min and, he says, Swann 'experienced a clear remote viewing' in its final phase. The Swann paper ran 'burst-firing and frequency-modulated (Thomas)' patterns, 'three different parameters for each, a part of our standard protocol (Cook, et al., 1999)', 5 min each, counter-clockwise at 2-5 uT, one 30-min exposure, and in the final configuration (T3) Swann saw the three experimenters 'as skeletons'. Its Table 1 gives pixel (point) duration / interstimulus time / commutator rate / change in rate: B1 and T1 1/1/20/+2 ms, B2 and T2 1/1/100/+20 ms, B3 and T3 3/3000/200/-2 ms. Commutator rate is read as the time on the first coil and the change as the change at each next coil, with the plain sign as in the Koren software patent: 20 to 34, 100 to 240 and 200 to 186 ms (216, 1360 and 1544 ms per turn, inside the 'about 200 and 2000 ms' rotations of Cook 1999). The lab's later notation reads '+2' as 2 ms shorter (20 to 6 and 200 to 214 ms; B1 would then take 104 ms per turn). persinger-swann-2002-table1 is the lab version of this session: the same timings and sign reading, without quiet intervals, with the exact Thomas table and the lab's 2-5 uT. Murphy publishes none of his own coil timings, point durations or gaps; he says only that the signals are 'chopped' into lengths and 'Some of them get longer as they go along, and some of them get shorter', which fits the table's rising and falling ramps, so giving the Shiva session the Table 1 values is an inference. Nor does he publish his phase or interval lengths: each configuration runs 5 min as in the lab, and the 10-15 min by which his session is longer than the lab's 30 min is taken to be the quiet intervals, here five of 2.5 min (42.5 min in all, an inference). Coils sit on Murphy's Shiva ring, one coil per site instead of Shiva's coil pairs: the first over the left frontal area (Fp1), then FT7, TP7, O1, O2, TP8, FT8, Fp2, counter-clockwise seen from above (left side front to back, right side back to front); no coils above the nose, directly above the ears or above the bony ridge at the back. The signal files are proprietary. Amygdala: the built-in accelerating burst of 230 points (the lab's burst-firing length, Ryczko & Persinger 2002), 6 to 30 Hz at 3-ms points; at the 1-ms points of B1 and B2 the same points play three times faster (18 to 90 Hz in 230 ms) with 1 ms between bursts, the format of Murphy's own 'High-Speed' signals (his ltp_1_1 page: 'One millisecond between signals, and one millisecond for each point'); in B3 a 0.69-s burst follows every 3-s gap. Chirp: Murphy uses his modulated 40 Hz chirp where the lab used its frequency-modulated pattern (he calls the lab's an earlier 'pulse named for its designer'; that this is the Thomas pattern is an inference). He says the chirp 'does not change in tone, but rather has longer and longer gaps between sections of the signal as they travel around your head', so a steady 40 Hz carrier plays and the coil-to-coil timing supplies the gaps, as in murphy-shiva-persinger-session; any modulation inside the original is not reproduced. The lab's pixel durations are used as hold steps (1 ms; 3 ms in T3, a coarse 40 Hz staircase); each chirp section lasts as long as the 849-point Thomas file at that point duration (849 ms in T1 and T2, 2.55 s in T3; an inference) and is followed by the interstimulus gap (1 ms; 3 s in T3); whether Shiva also slows its chirp at 3-ms points is unpublished. The lab used 2-5 uT (Swann) and about 10 uT (Cook 1999); this file defaults to 1 uT and the helmet stops at 5 uT, so it copies the timing rather than the lab strength (no independent measurement of Shiva's output has been found). Tsang 2004 also ran six 5-min configurations but with other timings (25 to 11 ms, persinger-tsang-2004-gamma-thomas), so it is not the template; the effective pattern of Persinger, Koren & Tsang 2003 (100 ms with 20-ms changes) is the B2/T2 timing. Evidence is rated 'claim': no test of this Shiva session has been published; the lab configurations it copies are single-lab (one subject, no sham, in the Swann study) and not independently replicated. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Changed in this revision: the timings now follow Swann 2002 Table 1 (previously a mix of Richards 2002, Persinger 2003 and Tsang 2004 values), the lab's point durations and gaps are applied to both signals, and the silences are 2.5 instead of 2 min. Not for people with epilepsy; stop at once if distressed.
setting: Dark, acoustically silent room, eyes covered, seated and relaxed without meditating or falling asleep. For effects during the session Murphy recommends the highest Shiva setting (92%) in sensory deprivation, 'especially silence'; the lab subjects sat blindfolded in an acoustic chamber.
schedule: At most once a week; never on consecutive days, and not back to back with the Persinger Session.

phases.name: 1 Amygdala (B1): 1-ms points, 1-ms gaps, 20 to 34 ms per coil
2 Amygdala (B2): 1-ms points, 1-ms gaps, 100 to 240 ms per coil
3 Amygdala (B3): 3-ms points, 3-s gaps, 200 to 186 ms per coil
4 Chirp, steady 40 Hz (T1): 1-ms points, 20 to 34 ms per coil
5 Chirp (T2): 1-ms points, 100 to 240 ms per coil
6 Chirp (T3): 3-ms points, 3-s gaps, 200 to 186 ms per coil
